doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Listening to own work; bad gigs
summary: She does not listen to her own records and shrugs off bad gigs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Do you listen to your own work much?

Just keep doing something that you hope is better. You keep wanting to do something different. Ask a musician what they’re most interested in, it’s what they’re doing right at the moment you know. That’s what interests you.
Is Joe a good critic of your work?
Sure. It goes both ways. It goes both ways yeah. We see inside each other pretty well.
Have either one of you ever done a gig or — how shall I phrase this — that turned out to be really like oh man, I wish I hadn’t done that?

Sure. Oh there’s always those things that happen. Absolutely. At least you have somebody to commiserate with. It happens, yeah. Sure. There are always events that happen that, oh just, this was a hard one or something like that. But you know, you just, you know you’ve got to pick yourself up and keep moving on, because if you’ve been at it long enough you realize that there’s always another day you know, there’s always another chorus, there’s always another opportunity to play another improvisation that’s going to make that one go into history.
Right. Help keep things in perspective. The high is that much higher I guess.
Yeah. It’s just time that teaches you that. You can get upset but it doesn’t last for too long.
